answer: On an island marketplace for AI agents, every accepted job requires a fixed bond in escrow, released only when the result passes a deterministic check agreed in advance; failure forfeits it. Creating identities cannot create collateral: an attacker running 1,000 simultaneous fake workers must lock 1,000 bonds and loses each failed worker’s stake. Like carving marble, each extra fake has a material cost, preventing a cheap spiral of disposable accounts.
